Compute the strong dependency and conflict graphs of a variability model

Source: R/generate.R
vp_generate.Rd

Reads a variability model written in UVL, or the Boolean formula of a model written in any other notation (a DIMACS file, such as those that KMax, KConfigReader, KconfigSampler or TraVarT produce from Kconfig and other languages), and computes every strong binary relationship between its features, that is, every relationship that holds in all the valid configurations:

Usage

vp_generate(
  input,
  output_dir = NULL,
  threads = 1,
  or_graph = FALSE,
  kernel = FALSE,
  atomic = TRUE,
  minimal = TRUE,
  check = TRUE,
  fail_on_check = TRUE,
  mig = TRUE,
  keep_dimacs = FALSE,
  tseitin = FALSE,
  strict_uvl = FALSE,
  translator = c("auto", "kmax", "kconfigreader", "kconfigsampler", "travart", "uvl",
    "generic"),
  tristate = c("merge", "builtin", "both"),
  nonbool = c("merge", "drop", "keep"),
  visibility = c("drop", "keep"),
  abstract_groups = c("merge", "keep"),
  synthetic_root = c("drop", "keep"),
  abstract = c("drop", "keep", "merge"),
  fixed_nodes = c("drop", "keep"),
  unnamed = c("drop", "keep"),
  unknown_names = NULL,
  decls = NULL,
  decls_unconstrained = c("ignore", "add"),
  keep_type_prefix = FALSE,
  strip_config_prefix = FALSE,
  keep_pattern = character(0),
  drop_pattern = character(0),
  drop_names = NULL,
  filter_at = c("input", "output"),
  max_matrix_memory = 2,
  representativeness = FALSE,
  ganak = "ganak",
  legacy = FALSE,
  quiet = TRUE,
  read = TRUE
)

Arguments

input

The path of a .uvl file (a feature model in the Universal Variability Language), or of a .dimacs or .cnf file (a Boolean formula in DIMACS format, whose comments c <number> <name> name the variables).

output_dir

The folder for the files of the run. By default (NULL) a new temporary folder, which R deletes at the end of the session; give a folder to keep the files.

threads

Number of threads for the solver. More than the number of cores is reduced to the cores.

or_graph

Also compute the at-least-one graph. It roughly doubles the work of the solver, and it is needed for everything that concerns leaving features out.

kernel

Also compute the kernel (see vp_kernel()).

atomic, minimal, check

Write the atomic sets, the minimal form, and run the consistency checks on the output.

fail_on_check

If a consistency check fails, stop with an error (the default) or only warn.

mig

Use a modal implication graph to skip solver calls (same graphs, usually faster).

keep_dimacs

For UVL input: also keep the DIMACS translation in output_dir.

tseitin

For UVL input: translate with the Tseitin encoding (auxiliary variables) instead of the straightforward one.

strict_uvl

For UVL input: a constraint that cannot be translated (not Boolean, or naming a feature that the model does not declare) is an error instead of a warning.

translator

The tool that made a DIMACS file, which decides which of its variables are real options: "auto" detects it from the comments of the file.

tristate

Tristate options X / X_MODULE of Kconfig: one node "X built in or as a module" ("merge"), X only ("builtin"), or both.

nonbool

Value variables of non-Boolean options: one node "P is set" ("merge"), none ("drop") or one node per value ("keep").

visibility

KMax visibility variables: "drop" or "keep".

abstract_groups

TraVarT abstract group features (_xor, _or, _alt): "merge" into their parent, or "keep".

synthetic_root

The synthetic root __Root__ added by some translations: "drop" or "keep".

abstract

UVL features marked {abstract} (the root included): "drop", "keep", or "merge" into an equivalent feature that is not abstract, if there is one.

fixed_nodes

Core and dead options as nodes of the graphs ("keep"), or only in their lists ("drop").

unnamed

Variables without a name comment: "drop", or "keep" (named v<n>).

unknown_names

Names that match no rule of the translator profile: "keep", "drop" or "error". NULL: "drop" for KMax, KConfigReader and KconfigSampler, "keep" otherwise.

decls

A file of declared option names, one per line: other variables are dropped.

decls_unconstrained

Declared names absent from the formula: "ignore", or "add" as isolated nodes.

keep_type_prefix

Keep the prefixes boolean_ and tristate_ (KconfigSampler).

strip_config_prefix

Strip the prefix CONFIG_.

keep_pattern, drop_pattern

Regular expressions: names to keep whatever the other rules say, or to drop.

drop_names

A file of names to drop, one per line.

filter_at

"input": dropped variables are never queried; "output": query all, filter when writing (for testing).

max_matrix_memory

Above this estimate, in GB, the minimal form and the checks use sparse algorithms.

representativeness

Count, with the model counter GANAK, the valid configurations and those that the graphs allow (turns on or_graph). Needs GANAK; see vp_representativeness().

ganak

The GANAK program: a path, or a name found on the PATH.

legacy

Reproduce the output of Strong4VM 1.x.

quiet

Print nothing but warnings and errors. FALSE prints the progress of the run.

read

Read the results and return the model (TRUE), or only return the prefix of the files.

Value

With read = TRUE, a model (an object of class vp_model, see vp_read()). With read = FALSE, the prefix of the files written (invisibly): the path of the output files without their ending.

Details

  • requires: selecting A always selects B (an arrow A -> B);

  • excludes: A and B are never selected together;

  • at least one (with or_graph = TRUE): every valid configuration has A or B.

It also finds the core features (in every product), the dead features (in none), the atomic sets (features that are always selected together), the minimal form of the graphs (vp_minimal()), and, with kernel = TRUE, the kernel (vp_kernel()). The results are written as files (Pajek graphs, lists, a CSV report and a JSON summary) into output_dir, and read back as a model, the object that every other function of the package takes.

This is the command strong4vm generate of the Strong4VM program; every option of the command line is an argument. Its other sub-commands are functions of the package: check is vp_check(), expand is vp_expand(), explain is vp_explain_conflict() and vp_explain_requires(), and diff is vp_compare() and vp_changed_links().

What the graphs cannot show

The graphs hold relationships between two features. A rule that involves three or more features at once (such as "A requires B or C", or "A, B and C cannot all be selected") is not in any graph, unless it implies a relationship between two features. Everything the graphs say is true; what they do not say may still be ruled out by such a rule. representativeness = TRUE measures how much of the model the graphs leave out (see vp_representativeness()).

See also

vp_read() to read the files of an earlier run; vp_example() for the models that come with the package.

Other reading: vp_classify(), vp_example(), vp_expand(), vp_features(), vp_functions(), vp_history(), vp_igraph(), vp_links(), vp_minimal(), vp_read(), vp_read_history(), vp_read_uvl_tree(), vp_representativeness(), vp_subset()

Examples

band <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
band
#> variplex model "miband3"
#>   features: 11 variable (the nodes of the graphs), 8 core, 0 dead
#>   requires: 36 arrows   excludes: 18 lines
#>   at least one: 3 lines
#>   atomic sets: 2 (of two or more features)
vp_features(band)
#> # A tibble: 19 × 2
#>    feature            status  
#>    <chr>              <chr>   
#>  1 Screen             variable
#>  2 TouchScreen        variable
#>  3 OLED               variable
#>  4 CapacityButton     variable
#>  5 ContactlessPayment variable
#>  6 MovementFilter     variable
#>  7 HeartRateSensor    variable
#>  8 BLEv40             variable
#>  9 BLEv42             variable
#> 10 BT40               variable
#> 11 NFC                variable
#> 12 FitnessMonitor     core    
#> 13 SleepTracker       core    
#> 14 VibrateAlert       core    
#> 15 Call               core    
#> 16 Notification       core    
#> 17 Pedometer          core    
#> 18 Accelerometer      core    
#> 19 Bluetooth          core    
vp_links(band, "excludes")
#> # A tibble: 18 × 2
#>    from               to             
#>    <chr>              <chr>          
#>  1 Screen             BT40           
#>  2 TouchScreen        MovementFilter 
#>  3 TouchScreen        BLEv40         
#>  4 TouchScreen        BT40           
#>  5 OLED               BT40           
#>  6 CapacityButton     BT40           
#>  7 ContactlessPayment MovementFilter 
#>  8 ContactlessPayment BLEv40         
#>  9 ContactlessPayment BT40           
#> 10 MovementFilter     HeartRateSensor
#> 11 MovementFilter     BLEv42         
#> 12 MovementFilter     BT40           
#> 13 MovementFilter     NFC            
#> 14 BLEv40             BLEv42         
#> 15 BLEv40             BT40           
#> 16 BLEv40             NFC            
#> 17 BLEv42             BT40           
#> 18 BT40               NFC            

# A Boolean formula in DIMACS format
f <- vp_generate(vp_example("eleven_options.dimacs"), translator = "kmax")
vp_links(f, "requires")
#> # A tibble: 8 × 2
#>   from             to              
#>   <chr>            <chr>           
#> 1 ACPI_INTERPRETER ACPI            
#> 2 ACPI_INTERPRETER NUMA            
#> 3 ACPI_NUMA        ACPI            
#> 4 ACPI_NUMA        ACPI_INTERPRETER
#> 5 ACPI_NUMA        NUMA            
#> 6 IA64_DIG         IA64            
#> 7 IA64_HP_ZX1      IA64            
#> 8 X86_PC           X86
